port.description: TCP port the daemon listens on. RFC 1413 reserves port 113; change only if running behind a port-forward.

bind_address.description: IPv4 address to bind to. Use 0.0.0.0 for all interfaces or a specific address to restrict which NIC accepts connections.

user.description: Unix user account the daemon drops to after binding. Must exist on the system; 'nobody' is a safe least-privilege choice.

group.description: Unix group the daemon drops to after binding. Pair with the user above; 'nogroup' grants no special filesystem access.

pid_file.description: Path where the daemon writes its PID on startup. Used by init systems and monitoring agents for process supervision.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for a client to complete an ident query. Lower values protect against slow-loris style connection exhaustion.

max_connections.description: Maximum simultaneous in-flight ident connections. Size this to your busiest mail/IRC server's concurrency — 50–100 is typical.

os_type.description: OS type token embedded in ident replies per RFC 1413 §2.7. Standard values are UNIX and OTHER; some clients require UNIX to parse the reply.

use_syslog.description: Route log output through syslog (recommended). Set false to log to a plain file instead; then set log_file.

log_file.description: Absolute path to the log file used when use_syslog is false. The directory must be writable by the daemon user.

log_level.description: Log verbosity: error (quiet), warn, info (recommended for production), or debug (verbose, for troubleshooting only).

response_mode.description: Controls what the daemon returns for a successful lookup. real = actual username; masquerade = a fixed fake name; noident = RFC NOIDENT; error = ERROR:UNKNOWN-ERROR. Use masquerade or noident to avoid leaking usernames.

masquerade_name.description: The fake username returned for every query when response_mode is masquerade. Ignored in all other modes.

enable_ipv6.description: Open an IPv6 listener alongside the IPv4 one. Required for dual-stack hosts that receive ident queries over IPv6.

deny_rules.description: Networks whose ident queries are rejected before any allow rule is evaluated. Use to block untrusted external ranges.

network.description: CIDR block to deny, e.g. 10.0.0.0/8 or 0.0.0.0/0.

allow_rules.description: Networks whose ident queries are explicitly allowed. An empty list permits all sources (after deny rules). Populate this to whitelist specific trusted networks.
